references.text: After Jesus' ascension, the believers continued to be in the temple, as described in Acts 2:46-47, where they gathered daily and with one accord in the temple, praising God and having favor with all the people.
In Acts 5:42 we see that the apostles continued to teach and preach in the temple every day, a continuation of the practice described in Luke 24:53.
Acts 1:14 shows that after Jesus' ascension, the disciples stayed together in prayer and supplication, which aligns with their constant presence in the temple praising God.
Psalm 135:1-3 calls for praising the Lord's name in the house of the Lord and in the courts of his temple – exactly what the disciples did when they were in the temple blessing God.
Psalm 150:1-6 is a concluding hymn of praise in the Book of Psalms that encourages praising God in his sanctuary. Luke ends his gospel in a similar way with praise in the temple.

The Gospel of Luke begins with the people praying outside the temple while Zechariah served inside (Luke 1:9-10), and it ends with the disciples in the temple praising God – a clear literary frame (inclusio).

Anna never left the temple, but served God with fasting and prayer night and day (Luke 2:37). The disciples' constant presence in the temple at the end of the gospel reflects this pattern of faithful worship.
Jesus himself taught daily in the temple (Luke 19:47), and after his ascension, the disciples followed his example by continually being in the temple.
Peter and John went up to the temple at the hour of prayer (Acts 3:1), showing that the disciples continued their practice of regular worship in the temple as Luke describes it in 24:53.
